stem: A sum of Rs 12100 is due at the end of 2 years. At a discount rate of 10% per annum compounded annually, what is the present value of this sum? [Given: (1.10)^2 = 1.21]

per_option_rationale.rationale: A slip in the division 12100 / 1.21 yielding 9800 instead of 10000.

Using simple discounting: 12100 - 2 * 10% * 12100 = 12100 * 0.8 would give different result; here subtracting only 1 year's interest at 10% gives 12100 / 1.10 = Rs 11000 approach confused further to give 10100.
Discounting for only 1 year instead of 2: 12100 / 1.10 = Rs 11000.

explanation_sections.punchline: Dividing the future value by the compound discount factor gives the exact present equivalent.
explanation_sections.approach: Name the formula: PV = FV / (1+r)^n. Map given data: FV = 12100, r = 10% per annum, n = 2 years. Use the hint (1.10)^2 = 1.21 to divide directly: 12100 / 1.21 = 10000.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always divide by the full compounding factor (1+r)^n, not by (1 + n*r) which gives simple-interest discounting.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 30 seconds using the given hint. Trap: only one year of discounting gives 11000.
